title: Purified Moringa oleifera Protein as a Terminal Disinfectant for Coagulated Domestic Wastewater: Benchmarking Against Sodium Hypochlorite, Cost, and Life‐Cycle Impacts
content:
Purified Moringa oleifera protein enables stage-specific coagulation and terminal disinfection of domestic wastewater. At the approximately 1.8-log E. coli endpoint, 50 mg/L PMOC was equivalent within ±0.3 log to 1.0 mg/L NaOCl. Life-cycle assessment shows that the current purification route imposes substantially higher environmental burdens, mainly from hexane and electricity.


ABSTRACT

Purified plant proteins are proposed as chlorine-free disinfectants, but their performance in real wastewater is rarely benchmarked against hypochlorite in the same matrix or translated into cost and environmental impact. We prepared a papain-assisted purified Moringa oleifera protein (PMOC; 86.0% protein) and tested it first as a coagulant, then as a terminal disinfectant, in domestic wastewater. Coagulation-stage conditions were evaluated with a 30-run face-centered central composite design (pH 3–11, 30–60 min, 0.50–2.00 g L−1). The selected condition (pH 7, 45 min, 2.00 g L−1) removed 86.1% ± 0.1% of total coliforms in three independent runs. The clarified supernatant was then split into supplementary-PMOC (25–200 mg L−1) and NaOCl (1.0–2.0 mg L−1 as Cl2) branches without further settling. After 30 min, 50 mg L−1 PMOC reduced Escherichia coli by 1.87 ± 0.04 log and total coliforms by 1.77 ± 0.005 log. In paired tests, these reductions were equivalent within ±0.3 log to those from 1.0 mg L−1 NaOCl (1.79 ± 0.01 and 1.72 ± 0.02 log), while 1.5–2.0 mg L−1 NaOCl produced greater E. coli inactivation. All PMOC doses met the national total-coliform limit without chlorine addition. A stage-specific life-cycle assessment (ecoinvent 3.12, EF 3.1) and a cost model showed that the current purification route has 83- to 133-fold higher climate burdens than NaOCl and alum–lime, driven mainly by hexane, grid electricity and NaOH. PMOC can therefore serve as a nonoxidant polishing agent, but its practical use depends on less solvent- and energy-intensive purification.
